components.note: 心 (heart) — feelings and thoughts, as in 想, 思, 急; 感 is to feel or be moved.
咸 (xián) is a loose sound clue for gǎn; 咸 also sounds out 喊 hǎn and 减 jiǎn.
氵 (water) — 氵 is water — dyeing means soaking in a liquid.
木 (tree, plant) — 木 is the plant dye material, steeped in water to make colour.

example.hanzi: 伤口感染了,需要马上看医生。
example.pinyin: Shāngkǒu gǎnrǎn le, xūyào mǎshàng kàn yīshēng.
example.english: The wound got infected — you need to see a doctor right away.
example.fact: Beyond the medical sense, 感染 extends naturally to emotions — 他的热情感染了大家 ("his enthusiasm was infectious to everyone") — much like "infectious" can describe a laugh or a mood in English.

examples.hanzi: 他感冒了,所以我怕被他感染。
examples.pinyin: Tā gǎnmào le, suǒyǐ wǒ pà bèi tā gǎnrǎn.
examples.english: He has a cold, so I'm afraid of catching it from him.

examples.hanzi: 她的笑容感染了在场的每一个人。
examples.pinyin: Tā de xiàoróng gǎnrǎn le zàichǎng de měi yí ge rén.
examples.english: Her smile touched everyone present.

components.note: 也 (also) — began as a picture (a vessel or snake; scholars disagree) and was borrowed for 'also'. A loose sound clue in 他 tā, 她 tā, 地 dì, 池 chí.
京 (jīng, high mound, capital) is a loose sound clue for jiù; going up to a high place fits 就 "to approach, to go to".
日 (sun) — on top; the usual explanation is sun over 正 "straight, correct": what is clear and straight is "right, is". A memory aid, not firm etymology.
讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 请, 谢, 话.
兑 (duì) is a loose sound clue for shuō; 兑 also sounds out 脱 tuō, 税 shuì and 悦 yuè.

example.hanzi: 他明天有事,也就是说他不能来了。
example.pinyin: Tā míngtiān yǒu shì, yě jiù shì shuō tā bù néng lái le.
example.english: He has something on tomorrow — in other words, he can't come.
example.fact: 也就是说 chains together four small, ordinary words (也 "also", 就 "then", 是 "is", 说 "say") into one fixed discourse marker — a good example of how Chinese often builds transitional phrases by fusing simple pieces rather than coining a dedicated word.

examples.hanzi: 他今天发烧了,也就是说,不能来上班了。
examples.pinyin: Tā jīntiān fāshāo le, yě jiù shì shuō, bù néng lái shàngbān le.
examples.english: He has a fever today, which means he can't come to work.

examples.hanzi: 我下周才有空,也就是说,这周不行。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiàzhōu cái yǒu kòng, yě jiùshì shuō, zhèzhōu bù xíng.
examples.english: I'm free only next week, so this week won't work.

components.note: 雨 (rain) — marks weather and moisture, as in 雪, 雷, 雾; 露 is dew.
路 (lù) gives the sound exactly: 露 lù (dew) or lòu (reveal).

example.pinyin: Tā lù chū le xiàoróng.
example.english: He broke into a smile.
example.fact: 露 means dew and, by extension, to expose: 暴露 (to expose), 露营 (camping), 露天 (open-air). In casual speech the verb is often read lòu: 露面 (to show up), 露馅 (to let the secret out).

examples.hanzi: 他的脸上露出了笑容。
examples.pinyin: Tā de liǎn shang lùchū le xiàoróng.
examples.english: A smile showed on his face.

examples.hanzi: 草上有一滴露水。
examples.pinyin: Cǎo shang yǒu yì dī lùshuǐ.
examples.english: There is a drop of dew on the grass.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand radical — 抛 is to throw, as in 抛弃.
廾 (two hands) — hands throwing something out: 弃 is to cast away.

example.pinyin: Tā pāoqì le zìjǐ de jiārén.
example.english: He abandoned his own family.
example.fact: 抛 by itself already means "to throw, to toss," so 抛弃 reinforces it with 弃 ("to discard") — pairing two near-synonyms to intensify a verb is a common Chinese word-formation strategy.

examples.hanzi: 有些人会随便抛弃小动物。
examples.pinyin: Yǒuxiē rén huì suíbiàn pāoqì xiǎo dòngwù.
examples.english: Some people carelessly abandon pets.

examples.hanzi: 我们不能抛弃那些需要帮助的人。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen bù néng pāoqì nàxiē xūyào bāngzhù de rén.
examples.english: We must not abandon those who need help.

components.note: 扌 (hand, 提手旁) — marks hand actions, as in 打 hit, 推 push, 拉 pull; 摸 is touching or groping.
莫 (mò) — close sound: 摸 mō. 莫 also sounds out 墓 mù and 幕 mù.

example.pinyin: Qǐng búyào mō xiǎogǒu.
example.english: Please don't touch the puppy.
example.fact: 摸 is to touch or feel for something, and it extends to finding things out: 摸清 (to figure out). 摸索 (to grope, to explore) and the slang 摸鱼 (to slack off at work, literally "to catch fish") are common.

examples.hanzi: 别摸我的头发。
examples.pinyin: Bié mō wǒ de tóufa.
examples.english: Don't touch my hair.

examples.hanzi: 他在黑暗里摸索着前进。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài hēi'àn lǐ mōsuǒ zhe qiánjìn.
examples.english: He groped his way forward in the dark.

components.note: 单 (dān) gives sound to 弹 dàn/tán and 蝉 chán; as a word it means single, alone, a list.
身 (body) — a person's body with a rounded belly. As a radical it marks body words: 躺 lie down, 躲 hide, 躯 body.

example.hanzi: 她今年三十岁,还是单身。
example.pinyin: Tā jīnnián sānshí suì, háishi dānshēn.
example.english: She's thirty this year and still single.
example.fact: 单身 describes relationship or marital status specifically, distinct from 一个人 ("alone," a physical state) — you can be 单身 while out with a big group of friends, or 一个人 for an evening while happily in a relationship.

examples.hanzi: 他单身多年,朋友都在帮他介绍对象。
examples.pinyin: Tā dānshēn duō nián, péngyou dōu zài bāng tā jièshào duìxiàng.
examples.english: He has been single for years and his friends are trying to set him up.

examples.hanzi: 我是单身,一个人住在公寓里。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ shì dānshēn, yí ge rén zhù zài gōngyù lǐ.
examples.english: I'm single and live alone in an apartment.

components.note: 田 here replaces 囟 (skull) in the older form: head over heart
心 (heart) — thinking and feeling, as in 想, 意, 感: 思 is to think over, with head and heart.
耂 (old) — shown in 老 old and 者; 考 first meant an aged person (the same word as 老), then to examine.
丂 (kǎo) gives the sound; also in 巧 qiǎo, 烤 kǎo and 拷 kǎo.

example.hanzi: 这个问题值得我们认真思考。
example.pinyin: Zhège wèntí zhídé wǒmen rènzhēn sīkǎo.
example.english: This question is worth thinking about carefully.
example.fact: 思考 pairs 思 ("to think") with 考 ("to examine, to test" — the same 考 in 考试, "exam"), giving the compound a more deliberate, analytical flavor than the everyday 想.

examples.hanzi: 睡觉前,我喜欢安静地思考一会儿。
examples.pinyin: Shuìjiào qián, wǒ xǐhuan ānjìng de sīkǎo yíhuìr.
examples.english: Before bed, I like to think quietly for a while.

examples.hanzi: 遇到问题时,要学会独立思考。
examples.pinyin: Yùdào wèntí shí, yào xuéhuì dúlì sīkǎo.
examples.english: When you run into problems, you need to learn to think independently.

components.note: 木 (wood) — trees and wooden things: 树, 桌, 桥; 板 is a plank or board.
反 (fǎn) is a near sound match (-an); same part in 饭 fàn and 版 bǎn.

example.pinyin: Lǎoshī zài hēibǎn shang xiě zì.
example.english: The teacher writes on the blackboard.
example.fact: 板 is a flat piece: 黑板 (blackboard), 木板 (plank), 滑板 (skateboard). 老板 (lǎobǎn) means boss or shop owner, and 板着脸 means to keep a stern straight face.

examples.hanzi: 老师在黑板上写了一个字。
examples.pinyin: Lǎoshī zài hēibǎn shang xiě le yí gè zì.
examples.english: The teacher wrote a character on the blackboard.

examples.hanzi: 他把木板放在地上。
examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ mùbǎn fàng zài dì shang.
examples.english: He put the plank on the floor.

components.note: 女 (woman) — women and family, as in 妈, 她, 姐.
子 (child) — a woman with her child: the picture of something good.
口 (mouth) — eating and speech: 喝, 吸, 吗; 吃 is to eat.
乞 (qǐ) is only a loose sound clue for chī.

example.pinyin: Zhè jiā cāntīng de cài hěn hǎochī.
example.english: The food at this restaurant is delicious.
example.fact: 好 + verb forms a whole family of evaluative adjectives this way — 好吃 (tasty), 好喝 (nice to drink), 好看 (good-looking), 好听 (nice to listen to) — each literally "good to [verb]."

examples.hanzi: 这个蛋糕真好吃,我还想再吃一块。
examples.pinyin: Zhège dàngāo zhēn hǎochī, wǒ hái xiǎng zài chī yí kuài.
examples.english: This cake is really tasty, I want another piece.

examples.hanzi: 妈妈做的饺子最好吃。
examples.pinyin: Māma zuò de jiǎozi zuì hǎochī.
examples.english: The dumplings Mom makes are the best.

components.note: 女 (woman) — a person kneeling with arms crossed; as a radical it heads many female and family words: 妈, 好, 姐.
王 (king) — three bars for heaven, people and earth joined by a vertical: the ruler who links them. As 玉 jade with its dot dropped it also marks jewels: 球, 玩.

example.pinyin: Nǚwáng zhù zài huánggōng lǐ.
example.english: The queen lives in the palace.
example.fact: 女王 (a woman who reigns as monarch in her own right) is distinct from 王后 (a king's wife) — English "queen" collapses both roles into a single word, but Chinese keeps them separate.

examples.hanzi: 女王坐在宝座上,看着大臣们。
examples.pinyin: Nǚwáng zuò zài bǎozuò shang, kàn zhe dàchénmen.
examples.english: The queen sat on the throne, looking at her ministers.

examples.hanzi: 孩子们表演了一个关于女王的故事。
examples.pinyin: Háizimen biǎoyǎn le yí ge guānyú nǚwáng de gùshi.
examples.english: The kids performed a story about a queen.

components.note: 氵 (water) — marks water and flowing things, as in 河, 海, 汤; 波 is a wave.
皮 (pí) is a loose hint for bō; 坡 pō and 破 pò share it.

example.pinyin: Hǎi lǐ yǒu hěn dà de bōlàng.
example.english: There are big waves in the sea.
example.fact: 波 is a wave in water and, by extension, in physics and in trouble: 电波 (radio wave), 风波 (disturbance), 一波三折 (many twists). It is also used in transliterations like 波兰 (Poland) and 波士顿 (Boston).

examples.hanzi: 今天的海里有很大的波浪。
examples.pinyin: Jīntiān de hǎi lǐ yǒu hěn dà de bōlàng.
examples.english: There are big waves at sea today.

examples.hanzi: 这件事引起了一场风波。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì yǐnqǐ le yì chǎng fēngbō.
examples.english: This matter stirred up a controversy.

components.note: 足 (foot) — 足 (⻊) marks feet and body positions, as in 跑, 跳, 路; 趴 is lying on the front.
八 (bā) — same sound — 趴 is pā; 八 is bā, like 扒 bā and 叭 bā.
下 (below) — a mark placed under a line, the mirror of 上 above.

example.pinyin: “Dōu pāxia!” jǐngchá dàshēng hǎndào.
example.english: "Everybody get down!" the police shouted.
example.fact: 趴 alone already means "lying face-down," so adding the directional complement 下 ("down") highlights the motion of dropping into that position — the same 下 that turns 坐 ("sit") into 坐下 ("sit down").

examples.hanzi: 小狗听到命令就趴下了。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎo gǒu tīngdào mìnglìng jiù pāxia le.
examples.english: The puppy lay down as soon as it heard the command.

examples.hanzi: 快趴下,别让他们看到你!
examples.pinyin: Kuài pāxia, bié ràng tāmen kàndào nǐ!
examples.english: Get down quickly, don't let them see you!

components.note: ⺼ (flesh, 肉月旁) — the body-part radical, as in 脸, 腿, 脑; 胖 is plump.
半 (bàn) hints at the sound: 胖 pàng is close, as in 伴 bàn and 拌 bàn.

example.pinyin: Tā zuìjìn yǒudiǎn pàng le.
example.english: He has put on a bit of weight lately.
example.fact: 胖 is blunt: calling someone 胖 can be rude, so politer speakers say 微胖 (a little chubby) or 丰满. For babies and pets, though, 胖乎乎 is a cute word for plump. The old reading pán survives only in the idiom 心宽体胖.

examples.hanzi: 他吃得太多，变胖了。
examples.pinyin: Tā chīde tài duō, biànpàng le.
examples.english: He ate too much and has gotten fat.

examples.hanzi: 我的小猫很胖，很可爱。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de xiǎomāo hěn pàng, hěn kě'ài.
examples.english: My kitten is plump and cute.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 说, 请, 谢; recognising something is naming it.
人 (rén) gives the exact sound, and also means "person".

example.pinyin: Wǒ rènshi tā hěn duō nián le.
example.english: I have known him for many years.
example.fact: 认 appears in 认识 (to know someone), 认为 (to think, to consider), 认真 (serious, earnest), 承认 (to admit). 认识 is for people and places you are acquainted with, whereas 知道 is for facts.

examples.hanzi: 我不认识这个字。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ bú rènshi zhège zì.
examples.english: I don't recognize this character.

examples.hanzi: 他承认是自己的错。
examples.pinyin: Tā chéngrèn shì zìjǐ de cuò.
examples.english: He admitted it was his own fault.

components.note: 革 (leather) — marks hides and straps, as in 鞋, 靴 boots, 鞭 whip; 勒 is to rein in or tighten.
力 (lì) is only a loose sound hint for lè.

example.pinyin: Tā bǎ shéngzi lēi de hěn jǐn.
example.english: He pulled the rope very tight.
example.fact: 勒 is lēi when it means pulling something tight (勒紧裤带, to tighten one's belt, a figure for economizing) but lè in 勒索 (to extort) and 勒令 (to order). The idiom 悬崖勒马 means to rein in the horse at the cliff edge, i.e. stop before it is too late.

examples.hanzi: 她把头发勒得很紧。
examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ tóufa lēi de hěn jǐn.
examples.english: She tied her hair back very tightly.

examples.hanzi: 他勒住了马。
examples.pinyin: Tā lēizhù le mǎ.
examples.english: He reined in the horse.

components.note: 土 (earth) — ground and place, as in 场 field, 城 city, 坐 sit.
也 (yě) is a loose sound clue for dì; 也 also sounds out 他 tā and 池 chí.
囗 (enclosure) — boundaries and surroundings: 国 country, 园 garden, 回 return; 图 is a drawn plan of a region.

example.pinyin: Wǒmen dǎkāi dìtú zhǎo lù.
example.english: We opened the map to find the way.
example.fact: 图 alone means "picture, chart, diagram" — the same 图 that appears in 画图 ("to draw a diagram") and 图书馆 ("library," close to "picture-book hall").

examples.hanzi: 这张地图上有这座城市所有的地铁站。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhāng dìtú shang yǒu zhè zuò chéngshì suǒyǒu de dìtiě zhàn.
examples.english: This map shows all the subway stations in the city.

examples.hanzi: 我用手机上的地图找到了这家饭店。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ yòng shǒujī shang de dìtú zhǎodào le zhè jiā fàndiàn.
examples.english: I found this restaurant using the map on my phone.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand radical — 按 is to press with the hand, as in 按摩 massage.
安 (ān) — same sound, different tone — 按 is àn; 安 also sounds out 案 àn.
灬 (fire) — fire and heat, as in 热 hot, 点 dot, 黑 black: light shining.
昭 (zhāo) is a close sound clue for zhào; 昭 itself means bright.

example.pinyin: Qǐng ànzhào shuōmíngshū cāozuò.
example.english: Please operate according to the instructions.
example.fact: 按照 introduces the rule, standard, or procedure an action follows; it overlaps heavily with 根据 in meaning, though 按照 tends to lean toward following something exactly, like an instruction manual.

examples.hanzi: 我们要按照计划完成这个项目。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yào ànzhào jìhuà wánchéng zhège xiàngmù.
examples.english: We need to complete this project according to the plan.

examples.hanzi: 你按照妈妈的方法煮一下吧。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ ànzhào māma de fāngfǎ zhǔ yíxià ba.
examples.english: Cook it using Mom's method.

components.note: 羊 (sheep) — traditionally 羊 over 大: a big, fat sheep was good, tasty and pleasing, hence beautiful. 羊 also appears in 样 and 洋.
女 (woman) — 女 marks women, as in 妈, 姐; 妙 first meant fine and delicate.
少 (shǎo) — loose hint — 妙 is miào; 少 also means few or little.

example.hanzi: 音乐会的旋律非常美妙。
example.pinyin: Yīnyuèhuì de xuánlǜ fēicháng měimiào.
example.english: The melody at the concert was truly wonderful.
example.fact: 美妙 typically describes things experienced through the senses — music, scenery, a voice — rather than a person's looks, where 美丽 or 漂亮 is used instead.

examples.hanzi: 海边的夕阳美妙极了。
examples.pinyin: Hǎibiān de xīyáng měimiào jí le.
examples.english: The sunset by the sea is simply wonderful.

examples.hanzi: 她的歌声美妙动听。
examples.pinyin: Tā de gēshēng měimiào dòngtīng.
examples.english: Her singing voice is lovely and pleasant to hear.

components.note: 扌 (hand, 提手旁) — marks hand actions, as in 打 hit, 推 push, 拉 pull; 揍 is hitting, as in 揍人 beat someone.
奏 (zòu) — same sound: 揍 zòu. 奏 also sounds out 凑 còu.

example.pinyin: Tā bèi bàba zòu le yí dùn.
example.english: His dad gave him a beating.
example.fact: 揍 is the casual, tough word for beating someone up, with 顿 as the measure word: 揍了一顿. 欠揍 means "asking for a beating". It is stronger than the neutral 打.

examples.hanzi: 他被人揍了一拳。
examples.pinyin: Tā bèi rén zòule yì quán.
examples.english: He was punched by someone.

examples.hanzi: 别打架，不然我揍你！
examples.pinyin: Bié dǎjià, bùrán wǒ zòu nǐ!
examples.english: Don't fight, or I'll beat you up!

meanings: Excuse me, I must be leaving now.

components.note: 夫 (man) — the main part. Dictionary reading: something 丿 slipping from a hand. Memory aid: a man 夫 dropping what he held — 失去 to lose.
阝 (mound, left-side form of 阜 hill) — hills and places: 院, 阳, 陆; 陪 is to sit by one's side.
咅 (pōu) is a loose sound clue; same part in 培 péi, 赔 péi, 倍 bèi.

example.pinyin: Wǒ yǒudiǎn shì, xiān shīpéi le.
example.english: I have something to take care of — please excuse me for now.
example.fact: 失陪 literally means "to lose [the ability to] accompany you" (陪 = "to accompany") and survives today only as this one fixed, polite formula for excusing oneself — never as a general verb for "leaving."

examples.hanzi: 我还有个会,先失陪了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ hái yǒu ge huì, xiān shīpéi le.
examples.english: I have a meeting, so please excuse me.

examples.hanzi: 各位慢用,我失陪一下。
examples.pinyin: Gèwèi màn yòng, wǒ shīpéi yíxià.
examples.english: Please enjoy your meal, I'll step away for a moment.

meanings: (of a shop, school etc) to shut down

components.note: 关 (close) — simplified from 關, a gate 门 with a bolt across it; 关 also means "concern", as in 关系.
门 (gate, door) — 门 is a gate, as in 开, 关, 问, 间; 闭 puts a bar across it, so shut.

example.pinyin: Zhè jiā shāngdiàn yǐjīng guānbì le.
example.english: This shop has already shut down.
example.fact: 关闭 sounds more formal and often more permanent than the everyday 关 — you 关门 (close the door) every night, but a business, a factory, or an era of history 关闭.

examples.hanzi: 晚上十点,图书馆就关闭了。
examples.pinyin: Wǎnshang shí diǎn, túshūguǎn jiù guānbì le.
examples.english: The library closes at ten in the evening.

examples.hanzi: 离开房间时,请关闭所有的窗户。
examples.pinyin: Líkāi fángjiān shí, qǐng guānbì suǒyǒu de chuānghu.
examples.english: When leaving the room, please close all the windows.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand radical — 擅 is acting on one's own, then skilled at, as in 擅长.
亶 (dǎn) — near sound — 擅 is shàn; 亶 also sounds out 坛 tán and 胆 dǎn.
长 (long, grow) — simplified from 長, an old person with long hair. Read cháng "long" or zhǎng "to grow, elder".

example.pinyin: Tā shàncháng tán gāngqín.
example.english: She's skilled at playing the piano.
example.fact: 擅长 takes a skill or activity directly as its object with no preposition needed (擅长 + 弹钢琴), unlike English "good at," which requires "at" before the gerund.

examples.hanzi: 他很擅长做饭,朋友们都爱吃。
examples.pinyin: Tā hěn shàncháng zuòfàn, péngyoumen dōu ài chī.
examples.english: He is good at cooking, and his friends all love it.

examples.hanzi: 你擅长什么运动?
examples.pinyin: Nǐ shàncháng shénme yùndòng?
examples.english: What sports are you good at?

components.note: 予 (give) — 幻 is 予 written reversed — giving turned around, an illusion.
心 (heart) — thought and feelings, as in 思, 感, 急: to think of someone.
相 (xiāng) is a close sound clue for xiǎng; 相 also in 箱 xiāng and 湘 xiāng.

example.hanzi: 孩子们喜欢幻想自己是超级英雄。
example.pinyin: Háizimen xǐhuan huànxiǎng zìjǐ shì chāojí yīngxióng.
example.english: Kids like to fantasize about being superheroes.
example.fact: 幻 ("illusory, phantom") also appears in 幻觉 ("hallucination") and 科幻 ("science fiction," literally "science-fantasy") — a character reserved almost entirely for things imagined rather than real.

examples.hanzi: 你不要总是幻想不可能的事。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ bú yào zǒngshì huànxiǎng bù kěnéng de shì.
examples.english: Don't always fantasize about impossible things.

examples.hanzi: 这只是我的幻想,不一定会发生。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǐshì wǒ de huànxiǎng, bù yídìng huì fāshēng.
examples.english: This is just my fantasy and may never happen.

components.note: 艹 (grass, plants) — 艹 marks plants — medicine was made from herbs, as in 药 and 草.
约 (yuē) — near sound — 药 is yào; 约 also sounds out 钓 diào.
牛 (ox) — cattle words like 牧 herd and 特 special; 物 first referred to livestock, then to things in general.
勿 (wù) sounds exactly like 物 — handy for recalling the pronunciation.

example.hanzi: 医生给他开了一些药物。
example.pinyin: Yīshēng gěi tā kāi le yìxiē yàowù.
example.english: The doctor prescribed him some medication.
example.fact: 药物 is the general, slightly clinical term for medicine as a category (used in pharmacology and medical reports), while plain 药 is what you'd ask for at an everyday pharmacy counter.

examples.hanzi: 这种药物每天要吃两次。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng yàowù měi tiān yào chī liǎng cì.
examples.english: You have to take this medication twice a day.

examples.hanzi: 有些药物不能和酒一起吃。
examples.pinyin: Yǒuxiē yàowù bù néng hé jiǔ yìqǐ chī.
examples.english: Some medications can't be taken with alcohol.

components.note: 犭 (animal; 犬 dog) — marks animals, as in 狗 dog, 猫 cat, 猪 pig; 狼 is the wolf.
良 (liáng) — close sound: 狼 láng. 良 also sounds out 粮 liáng and 浪 làng.

example.pinyin: Shān lǐ yǒu láng.
example.english: There are wolves in the mountains.
example.fact: Wolves in Chinese idioms stand for greed and cruelty: 狼心狗肺 (heartless), 引狼入室 (to invite a wolf into the house), 狼吞虎咽 (to wolf down food). The measure word is 只 or 头.

examples.hanzi: 晚上山里有狼叫。
examples.pinyin: Wǎnshang shān lǐ yǒu láng jiào.
examples.english: At night wolves howl in the mountains.

examples.hanzi: 他饿得像一匹狼。
examples.pinyin: Tā ède xiàng yì pǐ láng.
examples.english: He is as hungry as a wolf.

components.note: 心 (heart) — 心 is the heart, as in 想, 思, 念; 忍 is a blade 刃 over the heart — enduring pain.
刃 (rèn) — near sound — 忍 is rěn; 刃 is a blade with an edge marked by a dot.
又 (hand) — two hands pass a vessel: one gives, one receives; 授 shòu adds 扌 for "give".

example.hanzi: 他忍受不了这么大的噪音。
example.pinyin: Tā rěnshòu bu liǎo zhème dà de zàoyīn.
example.english: He can't bear such loud noise.
example.fact: 忍受 combines 忍 ("to endure, to restrain oneself") with 受 ("to receive, to undergo") — the same 受 found in 接受 ("to accept") and 感受 ("to feel"), all built around the idea of "taking something in."

examples.hanzi: 这么热的天气,我真的忍受不了。
examples.pinyin: Zhème rè de tiānqì, wǒ zhēn de rěnshòu bù liǎo.
examples.english: I really can't stand such hot weather.

examples.hanzi: 她忍受了很多痛苦,但从不抱怨。
examples.pinyin: Tā rěnshòu le hěn duō tòngkǔ, dàn cóng bù bàoyuàn.
examples.english: She endured a lot of pain but never complained.

components.note: 面 (face) — a picture of a face; extended to the surface or side of things, as in 外面 outside.
勹 (wrap) — a person curled around something; in 包 it wraps around a baby 巳, the original picture. 包 sounds out 抱 bào, 跑 pǎo, 泡 pào, 饱 bǎo.

example.pinyin: Tā měitiān zǎoshang chī miànbāo.
example.english: He eats bread every morning.
example.fact: 面包 literally means "flour-wrap" (面 flour, 包 to wrap) — a formation that reflects bread's history in China as a foreign-influenced food, distinct from the native steamed 馒头, which is made from similar dough but by a different cooking method.

examples.hanzi: 我想买一个面包和一杯牛奶。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng mǎi yí ge miànbāo hé yì bēi niúnǎi.
examples.english: I'd like to buy a bread roll and a glass of milk.

examples.hanzi: 这家店的面包刚出炉,又香又软。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā diàn de miànbāo gāng chūlú, yòu xiāng yòu ruǎn.
examples.english: The bread here just came out of the oven, fragrant and soft.

components.note: 一 (line) — dictionary reads 不 as a bird flying up toward the sky 一. The meaning 'not' is a borrowing, so the shape does not explain it today.
杯 (bēi) — a character that uses 不 as a loose sound clue (木 + 不). The sound is a hint only: 不 bù vs bēi.
亻 (person) — person radical; 仅 is the simplified form of 僅.
又 (yòu) — in the old form 僅 the sound came from 堇 (jǐn); 仅 and 谨 jǐn sound the same.
亻 (person) — person radical; 仅 is the simplified form of 僅.
又 (yòu) — in the old form 僅 the sound came from 堇 (jǐn); 仅 and 谨 jǐn sound the same.

example.hanzi: 他不仅仅是我的老师,还是我的朋友。
example.pinyin: Tā bù jǐnjǐn shì wǒ de lǎoshī, hái shì wǒ de péngyou.
example.english: He's not just my teacher — he's also my friend.
example.fact: 不仅仅 doubles up the "only, merely" character 仅 for emphasis; it's largely interchangeable with the shorter 不仅, but the reduplicated form adds a bit more rhetorical weight.

examples.hanzi: 这不仅仅是钱的问题。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bù jǐnjǐn shì qián de wèntí.
examples.english: This isn't just a matter of money.

examples.hanzi: 他不仅仅会唱歌,还会写歌。
examples.pinyin: Tā bù jǐnjǐn huì chànggē, hái huì xiě gē.
examples.english: He doesn't just sing, he writes songs too.

components.note: 木 (wood) — trees and wooden things: 树, 板, 样; 模 was a wooden mold or pattern.
莫 (mò) is close to mó; same part in 摸 mō, 膜 mó, 墓 mù.

example.hanzi: 这个孩子在模仿大人说话。
example.pinyin: Zhège háizi zài mófǎng dàrén shuōhuà.
example.english: The child is imitating how adults talk.
example.fact: 模 is mó in 模仿 (imitate), 模型 (model), 模特 (fashion model) and 规模 (scale). It is read mú in 模样 (appearance) and 模子 (mould).

examples.hanzi: 这个玩具是按照真车模型做的。
examples.pinyin: Zhège wánjù shì ànzhào zhēn chē móxíng zuò de.
examples.english: This toy is made as a model of a real car.

examples.hanzi: 他是班里的模范学生。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì bān lǐ de mófàn xuésheng.
examples.english: He is a model student in the class.

meanings: variant of 夥伴|伙伴[huo3 ban4]

components.note: 亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 们: 伙 is a companion.
火 (huǒ, fire) gives the exact sound; 火 also means fire.
亻 (person) — person radical — 伴 is a companion, as in 伙伴.
半 (bàn) — same sound — 伴 is bàn, like 半; 半 also sounds out 拌 bàn and 叛 pàn.

example.hanzi: 我们是多年的合作伙伴。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen shì duōnián de hézuò huǒbàn.
example.english: We've been business partners for many years.
example.fact: 伙 is traditionally linked to sharing meals or provisions as a group (as in 伙食, "meals, board") before broadening to mean any close companion or partner — a hint of its origin still visible in words like 伙伴 and 同伙.

examples.hanzi: 她是我最好的学习伙伴。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì wǒ zuì hǎo de xuéxí huǒbàn.
examples.english: She is my best study partner.

examples.hanzi: 我们想找一个可靠的伙伴一起创业。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen xiǎng zhǎo yí ge kěkào de huǒbàn yìqǐ chuàngyè.
examples.english: We want to find a reliable partner to start a business with.

components.note: 女 (woman) — a person kneeling with arms crossed; as a radical it heads many female and family words: 妈, 好, 姐.
又 (hand) — two hands 又 stacked: hands joined in friendship.

example.pinyin: Tā dàizhe nǚyǒu qù kàn diànyǐng.
example.english: He took his girlfriend to watch a movie.
example.fact: 女友 is a clipped, slightly more written version of the everyday 女朋友 — the two mean the same thing, but 女友 turns up more in writing (news, profiles) than in casual conversation.

examples.hanzi: 他的女友今天过生日。
examples.pinyin: Tā de nǚyǒu jīntiān guò shēngrì.
examples.english: His girlfriend's birthday is today.

examples.hanzi: 我女友喜欢养猫。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ nǚyǒu xǐhuan yǎng māo.
examples.english: My girlfriend likes keeping cats.

components.note: 用 (to use) — 甩 looks like 用 with the last stroke flicked out. Memory aid: use something up by flinging it away.

example.pinyin: Tā shuǎi le shuǎi tóufa.
example.english: He tossed his hair.
example.fact: 甩 is to swing or fling: 甩手 (to swing the arms), 甩头 (to toss the head). It extends to getting rid of: 甩掉 (to shake off), 被甩了 (to be dumped). 甩手掌柜 is a boss who delegates everything.

examples.hanzi: 他甩开我的手，跑走了。
examples.pinyin: Tā shuǎikāi wǒ de shǒu, pǎozǒu le.
examples.english: He shook off my hand and ran away.

examples.hanzi: 她甩了一下手里的雨伞。
examples.pinyin: Tā shuǎi le yíxià shǒu lǐ de yǔsǎn.
examples.english: She flicked the umbrella in her hand.

components.note: 世 (generation) — from 卅 (thirty): about thirty years is one generation, so an age or the world.
纟 (silk, thread) — 纟 is the simplified 糸 (thread), as in 红, 给; 纪 first meant the thread end, then keeping record, as in 世纪.
己 (jǐ) — same sound, different tone — 纪 is jì; 己 also sounds out 记 jì.

example.hanzi: 这座建筑建于十九世纪。
example.pinyin: Zhè zuò jiànzhù jiàn yú shíjiǔ shìjì.
example.english: This building was built in the nineteenth century.
example.fact: 纪 also means "to record" or "a period," as in 纪录 ("record"); 世纪 is generally thought to have been standardized as the translation for the Western "century" concept in the late 19th/early 20th century, when the traditional Chinese calendar had no equivalent hundred-year unit.

examples.hanzi: 二十一世纪是网络的时代。
examples.pinyin: Èrshíyī shìjì shì wǎngluò de shídài.
examples.english: The twenty-first century is the age of the internet.

examples.hanzi: 这座桥已经有半个世纪的历史了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zuò qiáo yǐjīng yǒu bàn ge shìjì de lìshǐ le.
examples.english: This bridge has a history of half a century.

components.note: 大 (big) — a front-facing person with arms and legs spread wide: big. As radical, 大 is in 天 sky, 太 too much, 夫 man.
广 (shelter) — a building, as in 店, 床, 度: hemp stalks drying in a shed. 麻 also gives sound to 磨 mó, 摩 mó and 魔 mó.

example.hanzi: 这个国家已经把大麻合法化了。
example.pinyin: Zhège guójiā yǐjīng bǎ dàmá héfǎhuà le.
example.english: This country has already legalized marijuana.
example.fact: 麻 on its own refers to the hemp or flax plant fiber long used in Chinese textiles and rope-making (also seen in 麻布, "hemp cloth/linen") — 大麻 narrows that general "hemp" character to the cannabis plant specifically.

examples.hanzi: 大麻的纤维可以用来做绳子。
examples.pinyin: Dàmá de xiānwéi kěyǐ yònglái zuò shéngzi.
examples.english: Hemp fibers can be used to make rope.

examples.hanzi: 这种大麻是一种古老的农作物。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng dàmá shì yì zhǒng gǔlǎo de nóngzuòwù.
examples.english: This hemp is an ancient crop.

components.note: 比 (compare) — two people side by side, one lined up with the other; to compare.
⺈ (bent figure) — the top part of 尔, a variant stroke group. 尔 is an old form of 'you'; today it appears mainly in foreign names like 比尔 Bill.
小 (small) — the bottom part and radical, as in 少 few. The shape does not explain 'you'; the character is now mostly sound-borrowed.

example.pinyin: Bǐ'ěr shì wǒ de Měiguó péngyou.
example.english: Bill is my American friend.
example.fact: 比尔 is a pure sound transliteration with no meaning of its own — 比 ("to compare") and 尔 (an archaic word for "you") are picked only for how they sound, the same method used for names like 比尔·盖茨 (Bill Gates).

examples.hanzi: 比尔今天在公司加班。
examples.pinyin: Bǐ'ěr jīntiān zài gōngsī jiābān.
examples.english: Bill is working overtime at the office today.

examples.hanzi: 比尔和他的太太下个月要去中国旅游。
examples.pinyin: Bǐ'ěr hé tā de tàitai xià ge yuè yào qù Zhōngguó lǚyóu.
examples.english: Bill and his wife are traveling to China next month.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — marks actions done by hand, as in 打, 拉, 提; 插 is to stick in.
臿 (chā) gives the sound exactly: 插 chā.

example.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ chātóu chā jìn chāzuò.
example.english: Please plug the plug into the socket.
example.fact: 插 is to push something in: 插头 (plug), 插座 (socket), 插花 (flower arranging). It also means to cut in: 插嘴 (to interrupt), 插队 (to jump the queue).

examples.hanzi: 请把插头插好。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ chātóu chāhǎo.
examples.english: Please plug it in properly.

examples.hanzi: 我们说话时，别插嘴。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen shuōhuà shí, bié chāzuǐ.
examples.english: Don't interrupt while we're talking.

components.note: 辶 (walk, 走之旁) — movement and roads: 过, 进, 送; 达 is to get through to, to reach.
大 (dà) is only a loose stand-in for the old sound part, so treat it as a rough clue for dá.
至 (arrive) — 到 is to arrive.
刂 is the knife form 刀 (dāo), a close sound clue for dào; 到 itself sounds out 倒 dǎo/dào.

example.hanzi: 他的成绩达到了录取标准。
example.pinyin: Tā de chéngjì dádào le lùqǔ biāozhǔn.
example.english: His grades reached the admission standard.
example.fact: 达到 takes an abstract goal, standard, or level as its object (达到目标, 达到水平) — for arriving somewhere physically, Chinese uses 到达 instead, with the same two characters simply swapped.

examples.hanzi: 你努力一点,就能达到自己的目标。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ nǔlì yìdiǎn, jiù néng dádào zìjǐ de mùbiāo.
examples.english: If you work a bit harder, you can reach your goal.

examples.hanzi: 今天的气温达到了三十五度。
examples.pinyin: Jīntiān de qìwēn dádào le sānshíwǔ dù.
examples.english: Today's temperature reached thirty-five degrees.

components.note: 辶 (walk, 走之旁) — movement and roads: 过, 进, 送; 运 is to move, then to be moved by luck.
云 (yún) is a near sound match for yùn.

example.pinyin: Wǒmen yòng kǎchē yùn huò.
example.english: We transport goods by truck.
example.fact: 运 means to carry and move: 运输 (transport), 运动 (exercise). It also means luck or fate: 运气, 好运, 命运. 运气 makes it clear whether luck is good or bad.

examples.hanzi: 我们坐船把货运到上海。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zuò chuán bǎ huò yùn dào Shànghǎi.
examples.english: We transport the goods to Shanghai by ship.

examples.hanzi: 祝你好运！
examples.pinyin: Zhù nǐ hǎoyùn!
examples.english: Good luck to you!

components.note: 回 (return) — a swirl or whirlpool drawn as nested squares: it turns around and comes back.
忄 (heart, 竖心旁) — feelings and mind: 怕, 情, 快; 忆 is remembering in the heart.
乙 (yǐ) stands in for 意 (yì) in the old form 憶, so it is a close sound clue for yì.

example.hanzi: 老人喜欢回忆年轻时候的事。
example.pinyin: Lǎorén xǐhuan huíyì niánqīng shíhou de shì.
example.english: Old people like to reminisce about their youth.
example.fact: 回忆 literally means "to circle back to memory" (回 "to return" + 忆 "to remember"), framing memory as something you revisit rather than simply retrieve.

examples.hanzi: 这张旧照片让我回忆起了小时候。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhāng jiù zhàopiàn ràng wǒ huíyì qǐ le xiǎoshíhou.
examples.english: This old photo reminded me of my childhood.

examples.hanzi: 那是我童年最美好的回忆。
examples.pinyin: Nà shì wǒ tóngnián zuì měihǎo de huíyì.
examples.english: That is my best childhood memory.

components.note: 阝 (city, place) — right-side 阝 is 邑 (city or place), as in 都, 那, 邻; 邮 was a relay post station.
由 (yóu) — same sound — 邮 is yóu, like 由; 由 also sounds out 油 yóu.
亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do: 你, 他, 位.
牛 (ox) — in the traditional reading, a person 亻 dividing up an ox: one piece, hence 件 as a measure word for items.

example.hanzi: 我今天收到了一封重要的邮件。
example.pinyin: Wǒ jīntiān shōudào le yì fēng zhòngyào de yóujiàn.
example.english: I received an important email today.
example.fact: 邮件 originally meant physical mail carried through the postal-relay system (邮) and was later extended, unchanged, to 电子邮件 ("electronic mail") — in casual speech, 邮件 alone now usually just means email.

examples.hanzi: 你回家以后,记得给我发邮件。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ huíjiā yǐhòu, jìde gěi wǒ fā yóujiàn.
examples.english: After you get home, remember to email me.

examples.hanzi: 请检查一下你的邮件里有没有这份文件。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng jiǎnchá yíxià nǐ de yóujiàn lǐ yǒu méiyǒu zhè fèn wénjiàn.
examples.english: Please check whether this file is in your email.

components.note: 日 (sun) — the sun beside the moon: two light sources, so bright and clear.
月 (moon) — as in 朋, 期, 有; here it brightens the night.

example.pinyin: Míngtiān huì gèng hǎo.
example.english: Tomorrow will be better.
example.fact: 明 means bright and by extension clear: 明白 (to understand), 明确 (clear), 明显 (obvious). 明天 (tomorrow) is literally "bright day". 明 is also the Ming dynasty (1368–1644).

examples.hanzi: 明天我们去看一个新电影。
examples.pinyin: Míngtiān wǒmen qù kàn yí gè xīn diànyǐng.
examples.english: Tomorrow we're going to see a new movie.

examples.hanzi: 这道题我明白了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè dào tí wǒ míngbai le.
examples.english: I understand this problem now.

components.note: 史 (history) — a hand 又 holding a record, the scribe. 史 sounds the same as 使 shǐ and 驶 shǐ.

example.pinyin: Wǒ xǐhuan dú Zhōngguó lìshǐ.
example.english: I like reading Chinese history.
example.fact: 史 is mostly in compounds: 历史 (history), 史书 (history book), 史前 (prehistoric), 史无前例 (unprecedented). 《史记》 (Records of the Grand Historian) by Sima Qian is the model for later Chinese histories.

examples.hanzi: 他很喜欢看历史书。
examples.pinyin: Tā hěn xǐhuan kàn lìshǐ shū.
examples.english: He likes reading history books.

examples.hanzi: 这是一部有名的史诗。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì yí bù yǒumíng de shǐshī.
examples.english: This is a famous epic.

meanings: to raise a hand to hit sb

components.note: 力 (strength) — effort and motion, as in 办, 助, 努. The part 云 stands in for 重 in the traditional 動, which was the sound clue.
手 (hand) — a picture of a hand with fingers spread. As a left-hand radical it becomes 扌 in 打 hit, 拿 take, 推 push.

example.pinyin: Bié dòngshǒu, xiān xiǎngxiang bànfǎ.
example.english: Don't resort to violence — think of a solution first.
example.fact: 动手 covers three related but distinct senses depending on context — starting a task, touching something you shouldn't, or throwing the first punch in a fight.

examples.hanzi: 有话好好说,千万别动手。
examples.pinyin: Yǒu huà hǎohāo shuō, qiānwàn bié dòngshǒu.
examples.english: Let's talk this through, and please don't use your hands.

examples.hanzi: 明天就要考试了,我们该动手复习了。
examples.pinyin: Míngtiān jiù yào kǎoshì le, wǒmen gāi dòngshǒu fùxí le.
examples.english: The exam is tomorrow, so we should get started reviewing.

components.note: 心 (heart) — mind and feelings, as in 想, 思, 感: 总 is simplified from 總, whose threads gathered everything together.
之 (of, go) — oldest form is a foot leaving a starting line: "to go". Now it is a literary particle meaning "of" or "it".

example.hanzi: 总之,这次旅行非常愉快。
example.pinyin: Zǒngzhī, zhè cì lǚxíng fēicháng yúkuài.
example.english: In short, this trip was very enjoyable.
example.fact: 总之 opens a sentence to summarize everything said before it — a cousin to 反正 ("anyway, regardless") and 简而言之 ("to put it briefly"), each adding its own shade of "in conclusion."

examples.hanzi: 总之,你要好好休息。
examples.pinyin: Zǒngzhī, nǐ yào hǎohāo xiūxi.
examples.english: In short, you need to get some good rest.

examples.hanzi: 大家说了很多意见,总之都是为了你好。
examples.pinyin: Dàjiā shuō le hěn duō yìjiàn, zǒngzhī dōu shì wèile nǐ hǎo.
examples.english: Everyone gave many opinions, but all in all they were for your own good.

components.note: 艹 (grass, plants) — plants and flowers: 花, 草, 茶; 英 first meant a flower, then outstanding, then hero.
央 (yāng) is a loose sound hint (-ng); also in 映 yìng and 殃 yāng.
讠 (speech) — 讠 is the simplified 言 (speech), as in 说, 话, 读; 语 is language and spoken words.
吾 (wú) — loose hint — 语 is yǔ; 吾 also sounds out 悟 wù.

example.pinyin: Tā de Yīngyǔ shuō de hěn liúlì.
example.english: She speaks English fluently.
example.fact: 英 in 英语 is a phonetic borrowing from "England" (英国), not a native description of the language itself — the same borrowed 英 shows up purely for its sound in 英镑 (pound sterling) and 英尺 (foot, the unit of length).

examples.hanzi: 我的英语不太好,但我在努力学习。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de Yīngyǔ bú tài hǎo, dàn wǒ zài nǔlì xuéxí.
examples.english: My English isn't very good, but I'm working hard to learn.

examples.hanzi: 你能教我英语吗?
examples.pinyin: Nǐ néng jiāo wǒ Yīngyǔ ma?
examples.english: Can you teach me English?

components.note: 能 (can) — originally a picture of a bear, a strong animal (熊 xióng adds fire 灬); "strong, able" gave "can".
不 (bù) is a loose sound clue for fǒu and gives the meaning "not".
口 (mouth) — speech, as in 吃, 唱, 问: saying no.

example.hanzi: 请问能否借用一下你的手机?
example.pinyin: Qǐngwèn néng fǒu jièyòng yíxià nǐ de shǒujī?
example.english: Excuse me, would it be possible to borrow your phone for a moment?
example.fact: 能否 is a formal, written equivalent of the spoken 能不能 — 否 alone means "or not," so 能否 literally compresses "can-or-not" into a single word, typical of bureaucratic or written register.

examples.hanzi: 请问明天能否安排会议?
examples.pinyin: Qǐngwèn míngtiān néngfǒu ānpái huìyì?
examples.english: Excuse me, could a meeting be arranged for tomorrow?

examples.hanzi: 我们要看天气怎么样,才能决定能否出发。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yào kàn tiānqì zěnmeyàng, cái néng juédìng néngfǒu chūfā.
examples.english: We'll see how the weather is to decide whether we can set off.

meanings: you can say that again (colloquial agreement)

components.note: 口 (mouth) — speech or assent: to say "OK". 可 is also a famous sound part: 河 hé, 歌 gē, 哥 gē, 何 hé all take their sound from it.
一 (line) — dictionary reads 不 as a bird flying up toward the sky 一. The meaning 'not' is a borrowing, so the shape does not explain it today.
杯 (bēi) — a character that uses 不 as a loose sound clue (木 + 不). The sound is a hint only: 不 bù vs bēi.

example.pinyin: “Jīntiān zhēn lěng a!” “Kěbu!”
example.english: "It's really cold today!" "You said it!"
example.fact: 可不 is a colloquial short form of 可不是 — both exist purely to voice enthusiastic agreement with what someone just said, functioning more like an exclamation than a full sentence.

examples.hanzi: “你也累了吧?”“可不,我今天走了一万步。”
examples.pinyin: "Nǐ yě lèi le ba?" "Kěbu, wǒ jīntiān zǒu le yí wàn bù."
examples.english: "You must be tired too." "Tell me about it, I walked ten thousand steps today."

examples.hanzi: “这家店的东西真贵。”“可不,我也这么觉得。”
examples.pinyin: "Zhè jiā diàn de dōngxi zhēn guì." "Kěbu, wǒ yě zhème juéde."
examples.english: "Things in this shop are really expensive." "Exactly, I think so too."

components.note: 木 (wood) — 木 is wood and trees, as in 桌, 板, 树; chairs were wooden furniture.
奇 (qí) — near sound — 椅 is yǐ; 奇 also sounds out 骑 qí and 倚 yǐ.
子 (child) — a picture of a baby with arms outstretched and legs bundled. As a suffix (孩子, 房子) it is a light noun ending.

example.pinyin: Qǐng zuò zài zhè zhāng yǐzi shàng.
example.english: Please sit in this chair.
example.fact: 椅 carries the 木 (wood) component because early chairs were built from timber, and the suffix 子 turns the character into a standard two-syllable noun — the same pattern behind 桌子 (table) and 杯子 (cup).

examples.hanzi: 他坐在椅子上看书。
examples.pinyin: Tā zuò zài yǐzi shang kàn shū.
examples.english: He sat on the chair reading.

examples.hanzi: 这把椅子坐起来很舒服。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bǎ yǐzi zuò qǐlái hěn shūfu.
examples.english: This chair is comfortable to sit in.

components.note: 干 (dry; do) — a forked pole or shield. It lends its sound to 肝 gān, 杆 gān, 赶 gǎn, 汗 hàn and 岸 àn.
氵 (water) — water and liquids, as in 河, 海, 汤; water means life: 活 is alive.
舌 (shé, tongue) is a loose sound clue for huó; also in 话 huà.

example.hanzi: 工人们正在工地上干活。
example.pinyin: Gōngrénmen zhèngzài gōngdì shàng gànhuó.
example.english: The workers are working at the construction site.
example.fact: 干活 is a casual, spoken term for manual or physical labor — here 活 means "work, task" (as in 活儿), not its more familiar sense "alive" — giving the phrase an earthier feel than the neutral 工作.

examples.hanzi: 他每天从早到晚干活,很辛苦。
examples.pinyin: Tā měi tiān cóng zǎo dào wǎn gànhuó, hěn xīnkǔ.
examples.english: He works from morning till night every day and it's hard.

examples.hanzi: 大家一起干活,很快就做完了。
examples.pinyin: Dàjiā yìqǐ gànhuó, hěn kuài jiù zuòwán le.
examples.english: Everyone worked together and finished quickly.

components.note: 革 (leather) — 革 is leather, as in 靴 boot, 鞭 whip; shoes were made of leather.
圭 (guī) — loose hint — 鞋 is xié; 圭 also sounds out 挂 guà and 佳 jiā.
子 (child) — a picture of a baby with arms outstretched and legs bundled. As a suffix (孩子, 房子) it is a light noun ending.

example.pinyin: Zhè shuāng xiézi tài xiǎo le.
example.english: This pair of shoes is too small.
example.fact: 鞋 carries the leather radical 革 on its left side, a holdover from when shoes were made primarily of hide, even though most shoes today are cloth, rubber, or plastic.

examples.hanzi: 进门请把鞋子放在鞋架上。
examples.pinyin: Jìn mén qǐng bǎ xiézi fàng zài xiéjià shang.
examples.english: When you come in, please put your shoes on the shoe rack.

examples.hanzi: 我想买一双新鞋子。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng mǎi yì shuāng xīn xiézi.
examples.english: I want to buy a new pair of shoes.
